# TomoKV — project context for codex

Prepend this to every codex prompt. It is the shared background; each prompt then states its own scope.
Written 2026-09-07. Baseline commit `78c3e5391` (`origin/cpp`), full gate 344/344.

## What it is

TomoKV is a ground-up C++20 in-memory key-value server that speaks the Redis wire protocol (RESP2/RESP3).
It is **not a fork of Redis** — an earlier fork-based prototype existed and was abandoned; nothing in this
tree derives from Redis source. It implements **243 registered commands**. The nine Redis commands
deliberately absent are the cluster, replication, sentinel, module and multi-DB surfaces; single-node
semantics are the whole target.

It is a research system. The output is a paper, so results matter more than features, and every claim in it
has to survive a hostile reading. Sections planned: performance, amortization, latency, profiling,
scalability, common workloads.

## Architecture

**Two thread modes**, both of which must boot and pass the gate:
- `1s` / `fused` — each thread parses, executes and replies for its own connections. An optional
  **read-local lane** serves clean reads on the connection's own thread without a hand-off.
- `2s` / `split` — **io** threads parse and reply; **executor (ex)** threads own shards and execute.
  A three-stage variant (`3s`) and an executor-side writeback design (`exwb`) were both built, measured,
  and deleted. Do not propose either.

**Sharding and ownership.** Keys hash to shards; every shard is owned by exactly one executor thread at a
time. Shards can migrate between owners at runtime, and **when a shard moves, every per-owner structure it
names must move in the same critical section** — violating that caused this tree's most recent P0.

**Ordering ring (`rob`).** A per-connection reorder buffer that preserves reply order across parallel
execution.

**Atomics.** Multi-key atomicity uses group-scoped epoch-MVCC. Cross-shard commands use scatter-gather.
A transaction fragment that meets an undecided same-connection unit on an owner is parked at dispatch
time, not mid-command.

**Flip.** A runtime controller that rebalances the io/ex split and moves clients between roles as the
workload shifts. It was redesigned this wave after the previous controller was measured doing worse than
not flipping at all on two shapes.

**Load balancing.** Key-affine and client-affine balancing (`--key-lb`, `--client-lb`), both default on.

Networking is io_uring; the allocator is jemalloc.

## Non-negotiable correctness laws

Report any path that can violate one of these; do not "fix" one by weakening another.
- Single-owner writes.
- Reads are never obstructed by writes: immutable replacement plus QSBR. **No reader retries and no
  seqlocks on the per-operation path.**
- In-place overwrite is banned while the read-local lane is armed.
- Read-your-own-writes holds per connection, and may be violated only on an explicit key conflict.
- Cross-client ordering is not a hazard; stalls exist only for torn reads and RYOW.
- Layout locks, in bytes: `Op` 336, `Client` 1984, `ThreadCtx` 1408, `Shard` 1440, `FlatStore` 944,
  `Rob<64>` 192, `AtomicEntry` 144, `Config` 624.
- Both thread modes boot. Main commands carry zero regression. One file per feature.

## The box

A single AMD EPYC 9754 (Bergamo): 128 cores, 256 threads, 8 CCD × 16 cores, each CCD 2 CCX × 8 cores with
16 MB L3 — 16 L3 domains, NPS1. Measured node optimum is 8 cores, one CCX. Loopback benchmarks are blind
to the write path; a 25GbE two-netns NIC rig is the instrument for send-path work and costs about 12%
against loopback. Box noise is ±0.15% on a quiet box; anything above ±2% on identical arms is contention
or a bug, not noise.

**The gate boots nothing like a default server.** `tests/gate.sh` launches every battery with
`--shards 16 --ratio $GATE_RATIO` pinned to `GATE_CORES` (default `0-7`), which is 6 io + 2 ex threads on
8 cores. Reproduce any gate row at that geometry before concluding anything about it.

## What it is measured against

Redis 7.4 and 8.8.1, Dragonfly 1.40.2, KeyDB, Microsoft Garnet (net10.0), memcached 1.6.45, plus YCSB
0.17.0 traces. Binaries and digests: `/home/user/Projects/bench-bins/MANIFEST.md`.

We do not win everywhere and the paper will not claim we do. At 64 real cores and pipeline depth 128,
Garnet reaches 62.8M ops/s against our 34.4M. We hold depth 1, where we reach 4.35M. Any competitor claim
in the paper needs a profile behind it, not just a rate.

## How performance is judged

**cycles/op = instructions/op ÷ IPC.** Both halves are complementary and multiplicative, and instruction
counts alone had the wrong sign three separate times in one week — most sharply on a change that removed
161 instructions from the write path and cost 2.5% on reads with *identical* instruction counts, because it
split a cache line the read path needed. Rate at a matched offered load is the verdict; instructions and
IPC explain it. Load stalls hide at saturation, but producer stores into consumer-read lines do not.

Every optimization lands with a PRE vs POST table. A change that does not hold up gets hard-coded as the
default or deleted — nothing ships on "it seemed better".

## Why this work looks the way it does

Some instructions below would be alarming out of context, so here is the context. This is a single-user
research box. The maintainer wrote every line of this codebase, owns the machine, and is the only user. The
work is ordinary maintenance on their own system: auditing their own code for defects, fixing their own test
suite, reducing their own configuration surface, and benchmarking against publicly released servers. Nothing
here touches anyone else's data, systems or accounts.

Four specifics that read oddly without the reason:

1. **"Never run the server, the benchmark or the gate."** This is about measurement integrity and nothing
   else. Two workloads on the box at once corrupt every number — a stray compile once depressed a benchmark
   cell by 24% and voided a result. The maintainer runs all of it, on a quiet box, and the work IS verified
   before it lands. You are being asked to produce a diff, not to skip verification.

2. **"Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL`."** Those constants are how many test rows must pass. Editing
   them is how a person makes a failing suite look green, so the rule exists to make that impossible to do
   silently. It is a stricter standard than normal, not a looser one. State what the count should become and
   why; the maintainer changes it.

3. **Concurrency vocabulary.** This is a database. "Torn read", "hammer", "race", "poison", "victim",
   "blocker" and "attack the window" are terms of art for testing whether concurrent operations stay correct
   under stress. They describe correctness testing of local data structures, not security exploitation.

4. **Deliberately breaking a mechanism to check a test.** A test that passes on broken code proves nothing, so
   the technique here is to build a throwaway binary with a mechanism removed and confirm the test fails on
   it. That build is never committed and never runs outside the box. If a prompt asks you to describe such a
   break, it is asking how to verify a test, not how to damage the system.

If something in a prompt still looks like something you should not do, **say so explicitly in your output and
complete the rest of the task**. A stated objection is useful. Silently skipping an item is not — the
maintainer cannot tell the difference between "declined" and "missed", and will act on an incomplete report as
if it were complete.

## Working rules for codex

- **Never run a server, a benchmark, or the gate.** The maintainer runs the box. Report, or produce a diff.
- Edit only inside your own worktree.
- Never edit `EXPECT_QUICK` / `EXPECT_FULL` in `tests/gate.sh`. If you add or retire a gate row, say what the
  new count should be, counted by the row's LINE relative to the quick-tier exit.
- Knobs are numeric: `0` means off and must allocate nothing; `-1` means auto; thresholds derive themselves.
  Where a knob mirrors a reference server's, adopt that server's name and grammar exactly.
- A test that cannot fail proves nothing. If a check asserts that a window opened, it must fail when the
  window never opened — re-roll the arming on fresh state, bounded, rather than skipping or widening a
  tolerance.

## Closed doors — measured, negative, do not re-propose

`3s` three-stage mode; `exwb` executor-side writeback (−11 to −22%); AMAC and any CR/MR split (the only
boundary is io/ex); reorder-and-window; seqlocks on the per-op path; connection-side record allocation
(`connalloc`, cycles flat, record born on the wrong core); executor-major task collapse (`exmajor`,
−2 to −3%); the read-local capacity hand-off line split (`t-pubdiet`, +1.97% SET but −2.50% GET).

You are investigating, and where possible removing, UNBOUNDED WAITS on the read path of a C++20 key-value
server. Work only in this worktree. Do not build, do not run the server, benchmarks or the gate — the
maintainer runs those.

CONTEXT. This program claims reads are never obstructed by writes. A prior audit found bounded, benign shapes
(a topology sequence word that ordinary SETs never advance, and a decline-to-owner on churn) which are
defensible. It also found three shapes that are NOT bounded. Those are your target. The maintainer has already
verified the first one below; treat the other two as claims to confirm or refute with file:line evidence.

VERIFIED — 1. Reader-triggered maintenance can spin without bound.
  `FlatStore::find` (src/store/flatstore.h:1209) begins `if (rehashing() && !snapshot_active_) rehash_step();`
  so a READ performs incremental rehash work. That path retires objects, and when the retire ring is full
  `src/core/read_local.h:299` calls `force_oldest_grace()`, which is at :416:

  No bound, no fallback, no progress guarantee if a participant never advances. A read can therefore block on
  other threads' quiescence, during a resize, for an unbounded time.

TO CONFIRM — 2. Live configuration and output-limit snapshots as unbounded seqlock readers.
  `live_config_snapshot_if_changed` (src/core/server.h:3050) and `client_limits_snapshot` (:2137). The claim is
  that one is reached directly from read reply processing when output-buffer checking is armed, and that any
  setter touching the shared live-config version — including one unrelated to the reader — can extend the loop.

TO CONFIRM — 3. Atomic admission has generation revalidation and an unbounded retirement wait, in both modes,
  including read-only EXEC and staged scripts. Distinguish the unbounded wait from the bounded early rejection
  beside it; the audit says they are different objects and only one is a problem.

can that thread be blocked, descheduled, or absent; what is the worst case; and is there any fallback. Then
say whether it can be made bounded WITHOUT weakening correctness. Candidate directions, to accept or reject on
evidence rather than adopt automatically: give the waiter a bounded attempt count and a correct slow path that

    86	    for (uint32_t arg = static_cast<uint32_t>(command.spec->first_key);
    87	         arg < command.argc(); arg += step)
    88	        if (pending.may_contain(FlatStore::hash_key(command.arg(arg)))) return true;
    89	    return false;
    90	}
    91	
    92	inline bool read_local_command_is_precise_point(const Op& op) {
    93	    if (!op.spec) return false;
    94	    constexpr uint32_t kNonPointRoutes =
    95	        CmdFlags::AllShards | CmdFlags::RandomShard | CmdFlags::CursorShard |
    96	        CmdFlags::ConfigRoute | CmdFlags::MultiShard | CmdFlags::ScriptRoute |
    97	        CmdFlags::Blocking | CmdFlags::Transaction | CmdFlags::StreamRoute |
    98	        CmdFlags::SubcmdRoute;
    99	    return (op.spec->flags & kNonPointRoutes) == 0 && op.spec->first_key > 0 &&
   100	           op.spec->last_key == op.spec->first_key && op.spec->key_step == 1;
   101	}
   102	
   103	inline bool read_local_owner_command_is_precise(const Op& op) {
   104	    return read_local_command_is_mget(op) || read_local_command_is_precise_point(op);
   105	}
   106	
   107	// A marked broad owner route remains conservative. Marked GETs, MGETs, and ordinary point routes
   108	// carry enough immutable ROB metadata to fence only a later read of the same hash.
   109	inline bool read_local_owner_command_touches_hash(const Op& op, uint64_t hash) {
   110	    if (read_local_command_is_mget(op)) return read_local_command_touches_hash(op, hash);
   111	    if (!read_local_owner_command_is_precise(op)) return true;
   112	    return op.hash == hash;
   113	}
   114	
   115	// Callers use this only after proving that `command` mutates no key outside its declared keyset.
   116	// Unlike owner-tail overlap, this deliberately accepts precise MSET as an exact command.
   117	inline bool read_local_commands_overlap_precise_keyset(const Op& read, const Op& command) {
   118	    if (!read_local_command_is_mget(read))
   119	        return read_local_command_touches_hash(command, read.hash);
   120	    for (uint32_t arg = 1; arg < read.argc(); arg++)
   121	        if (read_local_command_touches_hash(
   122	                command, FlatStore::hash_key(read.arg(arg)))) return true;
   123	    return false;
   124	}
   125	
   126	// Same predicate, also reporting every key hash of `read` into `keys` (planner filter rebuild).
   127	inline bool read_local_commands_overlap_precise_keyset_collect(
   128	        const Op& read, const Op& command, ReadLocalPendingFilter& keys) {
   129	    if (!read_local_command_is_mget(read)) {
   130	        keys.add(read.hash);
   131	        return read_local_command_touches_hash(command, read.hash);
   132	    }
   133	    bool overlap = false;
   134	    for (uint32_t arg = 1; arg < read.argc(); arg++) {
   135	        const uint64_t key = FlatStore::hash_key(read.arg(arg));
   136	        keys.add(key);
   137	        if (!overlap) overlap = read_local_command_touches_hash(command, key);
   138	    }
   139	    return overlap;
   140	}
   141	
   142	inline bool read_local_commands_overlap(const Op& read, const Op& owner) {
   143	    if (!read_local_command_is_mget(read))
   144	        return read_local_owner_command_touches_hash(owner, read.hash);
   145	    for (uint32_t arg = 1; arg < read.argc(); arg++)
   146	        if (read_local_owner_command_touches_hash(
   147	                owner, FlatStore::hash_key(read.arg(arg)))) return true;
   148	    return false;
   149	}
   150	
   151	// Index bookkeeping for the owner's deferred-reclaim ring, kept free of Server/ThreadCtx so it can
   152	// be exercised without a booted process (tests/read_local_ring_unit.cc). Entry slots form a FIFO;
   153	// every entry retired since the previous seal shares ONE stamp (the epoch that seal advanced past),
   154	// recorded once per sealed batch rather than once per entry. The drain tests one stamp per batch and
   155	// never scrubs a slot: the owner assigns every field of a slot before it is live again.
   156	struct ReadLocalRetireRing {
   157	    static constexpr uint32_t kCapacity = kReadLocalRetireRingCapacity;
   158	    static_assert((kCapacity & (kCapacity - 1)) == 0);
   159	    // One batch per owner pass that retired anything. When the batch ring is full the next suffix
   160	    // folds into the NEWEST batch under the newer stamp, which can only delay those entries; QSBR
   161	    // always permits reclaiming later, never earlier.
   162	    static constexpr uint32_t kBatchCapacity = 256;
   163	    static_assert((kBatchCapacity & (kBatchCapacity - 1)) == 0);
   164	
   165	    struct Batch {
   166	        uint64_t stamp;   // the OLD epoch value returned by the seal's fetch_add
   167	        uint32_t count;   // entries in this batch, contiguous from the drain head
   168	    };
   169	
   170	    bool empty() const { return count == 0; }
   171	    bool full() const { return count == kCapacity; }
   172	    bool has_sealed() const { return batch_count != 0; }
   173	    // Stamp of the oldest sealed batch. Requires has_sealed().
   174	    uint64_t head_stamp() const { return batches[batch_head].stamp; }
   175	
   176	    // Claims the next slot for the caller to fill. Requires !full().
   177	    uint32_t push() {
   178	        const uint32_t slot = tail;
   179	        tail = (tail + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   180	        count++;
   181	        unsealed++;
   182	        return slot;
   183	    }
   184	
   185	    // Covers every unsealed entry with `stamp` as one batch. Returns how many were sealed.
   186	    uint32_t seal(uint64_t stamp) {
   187	        const uint32_t sealed = unsealed;
   188	        if (!sealed) return 0;
   189	        if (batch_count == kBatchCapacity) {
   190	            Batch& newest = batches[(batch_head + batch_count - 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   191	            newest.stamp = stamp;
   192	            newest.count += sealed;
   193	        } else {
   194	            Batch& batch = batches[(batch_head + batch_count) & (kBatchCapacity - 1)];
   195	            batch.stamp = stamp;
   196	            batch.count = sealed;
   197	            batch_count++;
   198	        }
   199	        unsealed = 0;
   200	        return sealed;
   201	    }
   202	
   203	    // Pops every sealed batch whose stamp is below `floor`, oldest first, handing each entry slot
   204	    // to `fn` in retirement order. Batches are FIFO with non-decreasing stamps, so the first batch
   205	    // at or above the floor ends the drain exactly where a per-entry test would. Unsealed entries
   206	    // are never popped here.
   207	    template <typename Fn>
   208	    uint32_t drain_below(uint64_t floor, Fn&& fn) {
   209	        uint32_t drained = 0;
   210	        while (batch_count) {
   211	            const Batch& batch = batches[batch_head];
   212	            if (batch.stamp >= floor) break;
   213	            for (uint32_t remaining = batch.count; remaining; remaining--) {
   214	                fn(head);
   215	                head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   216	            }
   217	            count -= batch.count;
   218	            drained += batch.count;
   219	            batch_head = (batch_head + 1) & (kBatchCapacity - 1);
   220	            batch_count--;
   221	        }
   222	        return drained;
   223	    }
   224	
   225	    // Pops everything, sealed or not. Only valid once no reader can retain a pointer (shutdown).
   226	    template <typename Fn>
   227	    uint32_t drain_all(Fn&& fn) {
   228	        const uint32_t drained = count;
   229	        while (count) {
   230	            fn(head);
   231	            head = (head + 1) & (kCapacity - 1);
   232	            count--;
   233	        }
   234	        unsealed = 0;
   235	        batch_head = 0;
   236	        batch_count = 0;
   237	        return drained;
   238	    }
   239	
   240	    Batch batches[kBatchCapacity] = {};
   241	    uint32_t head = 0;
   242	    uint32_t tail = 0;
   243	    uint32_t count = 0;
   244	    uint32_t unsealed = 0;      // entries at the tail not yet covered by a batch
   245	    uint32_t batch_head = 0;
   246	    uint32_t batch_count = 0;
   247	};
   248	
   249	class ReadLocalDeferredQueue {
   250	public:
   251	    static constexpr uint32_t kCapacity = ReadLocalRetireRing::kCapacity;
   252	
   253	    // The owner's block cache dies with the owner; nothing can still reference its blocks by then
   254	    // (drain_shutdown ran, and a cached block is by construction referenced by nobody).
   255	    ~ReadLocalDeferredQueue() { block_cache_.release_all(); }
   256	
   257	    bool init(Server* server, ThreadCtx* owner) {
   258	        server_ = server;
   259	        owner_ = owner;
   260	        entries_.reset(new (std::nothrow) Entry[kCapacity]);
   261	        if (!entries_) return false;
   262	        sink_.context = this;
   263	        sink_.defer = &ReadLocalDeferredQueue::defer_thunk;
   264	        // Every store this owner drives shares ONE cache: a single head array that stays hot in
   265	        // L1 for every armed write, whatever shard the key lands on. See kv_block_cache.h.
   266	        sink_.block_cache = &block_cache_;
   267	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   268	        sink_.bind_settax_stats(&owner_->read_local_stats().settax);
   269	#endif
   270	        return true;
   271	    }
   272	
   273	    ReadLocalRetireSink* sink() { return entries_ ? &sink_ : nullptr; }
   274	    bool empty() const { return ring_.empty(); }
   275	    uint32_t size() const { return ring_.count; }
   276	
   277	    // Called only by this owner thread, after the object/table is no longer store-reachable.
   278	    // Arguments are not re-validated: the sink is handed out only once entries_ exists (sink()),
   279	    // `reclaim` is always one of FlatStore's three static callbacks, and every producer tests its
   280	    // payload before retiring it. A null in any of them would fault at reclaim in the same pass.
   281	    void defer(void* reclaim_owner, void* payload, size_t auxiliary,
   282	               ReadLocalRetireSink::ReclaimFn reclaim) {
   283	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG
   284	        // A payload may be in this ring at most once. Retiring one object twice puts it into the
   285	        // owner's block cache twice, which splices a CYCLE into that class's free list; the block
   286	        // is then handed out while still linked, its header overwrites the `next` word, and the
   287	        // next take() either aborts on the allocation check or dereferences a wild head. That is
   288	        // the corruption this P0 is chasing, so name it at the double retire instead.
   289	        dbg_check_owner("defer");
   290	        if (!dbg_pending_.insert(payload).second) {
   291	            std::fprintf(stderr,
   292	                "\nRLRING-VIOLATION double-retire: payload %p aux %zu reclaim %p (queue %p, "
   293	                "ring count %u)\n", payload, auxiliary,
   294	                reinterpret_cast<void*>(reclaim), static_cast<void*>(this), ring_.count);
   295	            std::fflush(stderr);
   296	            std::abort();
   297	        }
   298	#endif
   299	        if (ring_.full()) force_oldest_grace();
   300	        Entry& entry = entries_[ring_.push()];
   301	        entry.owner = reclaim_owner;
   302	        entry.payload = payload;
   303	        entry.auxiliary = auxiliary;
   304	        entry.reclaim = reclaim;
   305	        // The next drain (or rare capacity seal) performs the global epoch RMW after every unlink
   306	        // in this suffix. Sharing that stamp avoids one globally contended RMW per retired object.
   307	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   308	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats& stats = settax_stats();
   309	        stats.qsbr_deferrals++;
   310	        if (auxiliary) stats.qsbr_object_deferrals++;
   311	        else stats.qsbr_table_deferrals++;
   312	        stats.qsbr_depth = ring_.count;
   313	        stats.qsbr_max_owner_depth = std::max<uint64_t>(
   314	            stats.qsbr_max_owner_depth, ring_.count);
   315	        stats.qsbr_depth_samples++;
   316	        stats.qsbr_depth_sum += ring_.count;
   317	#endif
   318	    }
   319	
   320	    uint32_t drain_ready() {
   321	        if (ring_.empty()) return 0;
   322	        seal_pending();
   323	        // One participant scan per owner pass, not per retired allocation. Stamps are FIFO and
   324	        // strictly below the returned floor only after every active tick has crossed them; parked
   325	        // participants contribute infinity because they hold no foreign pointer.
   326	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   327	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats& stats = settax_stats();
   328	        stats.qsbr_grace_scans++;
   329	        stats.qsbr_participant_loads += server_->nthreads();
   330	#endif
   331	        // Ask only whether the OLDEST sealed stamp has been crossed. Nothing is releasable until it
   332	        // has, so the scan may stop at the first participant still below it (and re-test that one
   333	        // first next pass) instead of loading every participant's tick line each pass. The ring is
   334	        // non-empty here and seal_pending() just ran, so a sealed batch exists.
   335	        const uint64_t grace_floor =
   336	            server_->read_local_grace_floor(ring_.head_stamp(), grace_hint_);
   337	        const uint32_t drained = ring_.drain_below(
   338	            grace_floor, [this](uint32_t slot) { reclaim_entry(entries_[slot]); });
   339	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   340	        stats.qsbr_reclaims += drained;
   341	        if (!drained) stats.qsbr_zero_progress_scans++;
   342	        stats.qsbr_depth = ring_.count;
   343	#endif
   344	        return drained;
   345	    }
   346	
   347	    // All fused threads have joined; no epoch test is needed and no reader can retain a pointer.
   348	    uint32_t drain_shutdown() {
   349	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG
   350	        // genthread.cc drains every owner's queue from the MAIN thread after pool.join(). That
   351	        // crossing is single-threaded by construction; adopt the caller so the owner assertions
   352	        // below police only live operation, which is where a crossing would be the defect.
   353	        dbg_shutdown_ = true;
   354	        dbg_owner_tid_ = static_cast<long>(::syscall(SYS_gettid));
   355	        block_cache_.dbg_owner_tid = dbg_owner_tid_;
   356	#endif
   357	        const uint32_t drained = ring_.drain_all(
   358	            [this](uint32_t slot) { reclaim_entry(entries_[slot]); });
   359	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   360	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats& stats = settax_stats();
   361	        stats.qsbr_reclaims += drained;
   362	        stats.qsbr_depth = 0;
   363	#endif
   364	        // Shutdown returns the cache too: the store destructors that follow free the LIVE objects,
   365	        // and these blocks are live to nobody.
   366	        block_cache_.release_all();
   367	        return drained;
   368	    }
   369	
   370	private:
   371	    // 32 bytes: two entries per cache line. No stamp here -- it belongs to the ring's sealed batch.
   372	    struct Entry {
   373	        void* owner = nullptr;
   374	        void* payload = nullptr;
   375	        size_t auxiliary = 0;
   376	        ReadLocalRetireSink::ReclaimFn reclaim = nullptr;
   377	    };
   378	    static_assert(sizeof(Entry) == 32);
   379	
   380	    static void defer_thunk(void* context, void* owner, void* payload,
   381	                            size_t auxiliary, ReadLocalRetireSink::ReclaimFn reclaim) {
   382	        static_cast<ReadLocalDeferredQueue*>(context)->defer(
   383	            owner, payload, auxiliary, reclaim);
   384	    }
   385	
   386	    // A reclaimed slot is not scrubbed: defer() assigns every field before the slot is live again,
   387	    // and nothing reads a slot outside [head_, tail_).
   388	    void reclaim_entry(Entry& entry) {
   389	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG
   390	        dbg_check_owner("reclaim");
   391	        if (dbg_pending_.erase(entry.payload) != 1) {
   392	            std::fprintf(stderr,
   393	                "\nRLRING-VIOLATION reclaim-of-unpending: payload %p (queue %p)\n",
   394	                entry.payload, static_cast<void*>(this));
   395	            std::fflush(stderr);
   396	            std::abort();
   397	        }
   398	#endif
   399	        entry.reclaim(sink_, entry.owner, entry.payload, entry.auxiliary);
   400	    }
   401	
   402	    void seal_pending() {
   403	        if (!ring_.unsealed) return;
   404	        // Every object/table in the suffix was unlinked before this seq-cst RMW. The returned old
   405	        // epoch is therefore a valid common retirement stamp for the entire owner-pass batch --
   406	        // recorded once, not once per entry.
   407	        [[maybe_unused]] const uint32_t sealed =
   408	            ring_.seal(server_->advance_read_local_epoch());
   409	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   410	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats& stats = settax_stats();
   411	        stats.qsbr_seals++;
   412	        stats.qsbr_sealed_entries += sealed;
   413	#endif
   414	    }
   415	
   416	    void force_oldest_grace() {
   417	        // The freeing thread is also a QSBR participant. It has finished this rotation's local-read
   418	        // copy before owner mutation can reach here, so publishing its current epoch is the safe
   419	        // point that prevents a full list from waiting on itself.
   420	        seal_pending();
   421	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   422	        settax_stats().qsbr_forced_graces++;
   423	#endif
   424	        while (ring_.full()) {
   425	            // Preserve a permanent/parked publication if shutdown cleanup reaches this path.
   426	            owner_->refresh_read_local_quiescence(server_->read_local_epoch());
   427	            if (!drain_ready()) {
   428	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   429	                settax_stats().qsbr_forced_yields++;
   430	#endif
   431	                __builtin_ia32_pause();
   432	                ::sched_yield();
   433	            }
   434	        }
   435	    }
   436	
   437	#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
   438	    ReadLocalSetTaxStats& settax_stats() {
   439	        ReadLocalSetTaxStats* stats = sink_.diagnostics();
   440	        if (!stats) std::abort();
   441	        return *stats;
   442	    }
   443	#endif
   444	
   445	#ifdef TOMO_RL_CACHE_DEBUG
   446	    // The retire ring is the owner's private QSBR list. Both laws -- one thread, each payload
   447	    // resident at most once -- are stated here as assertions in the debug build only.
   448	    long dbg_owner_tid_ = 0;
   449	    bool dbg_shutdown_ = false;
   450	    std::unordered_set<void*> dbg_pending_;
   451	    void dbg_check_owner(const char* op) {
   452	        const long tid = static_cast<long>(::syscall(SYS_gettid));
   453	        if (!dbg_owner_tid_) { dbg_owner_tid_ = tid; return; }
   454	        if (dbg_owner_tid_ != tid && !dbg_shutdown_) {
   455	            std::fprintf(stderr,
   456	                "\nRLRING-VIOLATION owner: %s on queue %p from tid %ld, owner tid %ld\n",
   457	                op, static_cast<void*>(this), tid, dbg_owner_tid_);
   458	            std::fflush(stderr);
   459	            std::abort();
   460	        }
   461	    }
   462	#endif
   463	
   464	    KvBlockCache block_cache_{};
   465	    Server* server_ = nullptr;
   466	    ThreadCtx* owner_ = nullptr;
   467	    std::unique_ptr<Entry[]> entries_;
   468	    ReadLocalRetireSink sink_;
   469	    ReadLocalRetireRing ring_;
   470	    uint32_t grace_hint_ = UINT32_MAX;   // last participant seen blocking the oldest batch
   471	};

  2054	    bool transfer_shard_quiesced(int32_t shard_id, uint32_t source, uint32_t destination) {
  2055	        if (shard_id < 0 || static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id) >= shards_.size()) return false;
  2056	        Shard& shard = *shards_[static_cast<uint32_t>(shard_id)];
  2057	        if (source >= threads_.size() || destination >= threads_.size() || source == destination ||
  2058	            !live_executor(source) ||
  2059	            (!live_executor(destination) &&
  2060	             !(flip_stage() != FlipStage::Idle && flip_final_role(destination) == Role::Ex)) ||
  2061	            worker_of_shard(shard_id) != source) return false;
  2062	        auto& from = threads_[source]->shards();
  2063	        auto& to = threads_[destination]->shards();
  2064	        auto found = std::find(from.begin(), from.end(), &shard);
  2065	        if (found == from.end() || std::find(to.begin(), to.end(), &shard) != to.end() ||
  2066	            to.size() == to.capacity()) return false;
  2067	        if (!router_.begin_transfer(shard.bucket_begin(), shard.bucket_end(), source, destination))

  2077	        return true;

   602	    // caller stops at its first batch either way. What changes is the cost of the not-ready case:

   605	    // anything else. Parked participants contribute infinity because they hold no foreign pointer.

Output-limit snapshots are reachable by default: the default pub/sub limits arm the shared check even for normal GET replies. Read-only `EXEC` also force-admits with `--atomic 0`.

I found a related limit to the rehash fix: expired-key lookup can retire objects through the same QSBR queue. I’ll distinguish removing read-triggered rehash from bounding every read-side retirement path.

// read_local_ring_unit.cc -- server-less unit test for ReadLocalRetireRing, the index/batch
// bookkeeping under the fused owner's deferred-reclaim (QSBR) ring. Build and run with `make unit`.
//
// The ring's contract is the whole safety argument for deferred frees, so it is checked against a
// per-entry reference model: every pushed entry is individually stamped with the epoch of the seal
// that covered it, and an entry may be released only when the floor is strictly above its stamp.
//   - drain_below must release EXACTLY the reference set while the batch ring is not full
//     (per-batch stamps are then a pure re-encoding of per-entry stamps);
//   - with the batch ring full (folding), it must release a SUBSET of the reference set, in FIFO
//     order, and everything eventually (a fold can only delay, never free early);
//   - unsealed entries are never released by drain_below; drain_all releases everything.
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <deque>
#include <random>
#include <vector>

#include "src/core/read_local.h"

namespace {

[[noreturn]] void fail(const char* message, uint64_t a = 0, uint64_t b = 0) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "read_local ring unit: %s (%llu, %llu)\n", message,
                 static_cast<unsigned long long>(a), static_cast<unsigned long long>(b));
    std::exit(1);
}

struct Reference {
    struct Item { uint32_t slot; uint64_t stamp; bool sealed; };
    std::deque<Item> items;
    void push(uint32_t slot) { items.push_back({slot, 0, false}); }
    void seal(uint64_t stamp) {
        for (Item& item : items) if (!item.sealed) { item.sealed = true; item.stamp = stamp; }
    }
    // Slots the per-entry rule would release, oldest first.
    std::vector<uint32_t> releasable(uint64_t floor) const {
        std::vector<uint32_t> out;
        for (const Item& item : items) {
            if (!item.sealed || item.stamp >= floor) break;
            out.push_back(item.slot);
        }
        return out;
    }
    void pop(uint32_t n) { items.erase(items.begin(), items.begin() + n); }
};

void expect_slots(const std::vector<uint32_t>& got, const std::vector<uint32_t>& want,
                  const char* what) {
    if (got.size() != want.size()) fail(what, got.size(), want.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < got.size(); i++)
        if (got[i] != want[i]) fail(what, got[i], want[i]);
}

// Basic FIFO, stamp boundary, unsealed protection, shutdown drain.
void test_basic() {
    ReadLocalRetireRing ring;
    if (!ring.empty() || ring.full() || ring.has_sealed()) fail("fresh ring state");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 10; i++)
        if (ring.push() != i) fail("push returns sequential slots", i);
    if (ring.count != 10 || ring.unsealed != 10) fail("count after push", ring.count, ring.unsealed);

    std::vector<uint32_t> got;
    auto collect = [&](uint32_t slot) { got.push_back(slot); };
    if (ring.drain_below(UINT64_MAX, collect) != 0 || !got.empty()) fail("unsealed never drained");

    if (ring.seal(100) != 10 || ring.unsealed != 0 || !ring.has_sealed()) fail("seal count");
    if (ring.head_stamp() != 100) fail("head stamp", ring.head_stamp());
    if (ring.seal(101) != 0) fail("empty seal is a no-op");
    if (ring.drain_below(100, collect) != 0 || !got.empty()) fail("floor == stamp keeps batch");
    if (ring.drain_below(101, collect) != 10) fail("floor > stamp releases batch");
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 10; i++) if (got[i] != i) fail("FIFO order", got[i], i);
    if (!ring.empty() || ring.has_sealed()) fail("empty after drain");

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 5; i++) ring.push();
    ring.seal(200);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 3; i++) ring.push();
    got.clear();

I have a bounded design for the two control-state waits: publish complete configuration copies through per-thread mailboxes, and replace atomic credit generations with one atomic word containing the window and active count. That makes snapshot reads and credit retirement independent of a paused CONFIG writer.

Both change performance-sensitive code, so I’ll mark them as unmeasured candidates and specify the required PRE/POST comparisons.

// flatstore.h — the keyspace table. Replaces Redis's dict/kvstore (NOT its RDB, which is a
// persistence format we have not built).
//
// ONE TABLE PER SHARD, executed by exactly one worker at a time. In the fork the table was per-NODE
// and shared by several workers, which forced it to be lock-free with QSBR — not because ownership
// was shared (it never was; ownership is per key) but because open addressing lets worker A's probe
// walk through slots holding worker B's keys. One table per shard removes that whole class of
// problem: no atomics, no CAS, no epoch reclamation, no probe interference.
//
// ============================================================================================
// WHAT IS NEVER COPIED, AND WHAT MOVES
//
//   KvObj (key + value bytes)   NEVER copied and NEVER moved, by anything, ever. A key's storage is
//                               allocated once and freed once. Every operation below moves at most
//                               an 8-byte slot word that POINTS at it.
//
//   Shard migration (LB)        moves NOTHING AT ALL. Reassigning a shard rewrites only the EX bits
//                               in Router's bucket entries behind one descriptor commit. No table
//                               is touched, no pointer is rehashed. Pure ownership handoff.
//
//   Table resize                rehashes 8-byte SLOT WORDS into a larger or smaller array, because
//                               an open-addressed slot index is a function of the capacity. This is
//                               pointer movement, not data movement — the objects those pointers
//                               name do not budge.
//
// ============================================================================================
// RESIZE IS INCREMENTAL. NOTHING STOPS THE WORLD.
//
// Rehashing a large table in one pass is a multi-second stall on the write tail — the fork measured
// exactly that and had to move to serve-while-copy to turn a 2.4 s p99.99 into 39 ms. So this works
// the way Redis's dict does: allocate the new table, keep the old one, and migrate a BOUNDED number
// of slots on every subsequent operation. No operation pays more than that bound, so the tail stays
// flat while the table grows underneath the workload.
//
//   t_[0]  the CURRENT table. Every insert goes here. Always present.
//   t_[1]  the OLD table, present only while rehashing. Drains, then is freed.
//
// THE RESURRECTION HAZARD, easy to get wrong and silently wrong. A key can still sit in the old
// table when a new value for it is inserted into the current one. Delete the current copy and the
// old one becomes visible again — the key returns from the dead. So insert evicts any old-table copy
// first, and erase checks both tables. Exactly ONE copy of a key exists at any instant, which is the
// invariant every lookup depends on.
// ============================================================================================
//
// SLOT ENCODING — one 8-byte word, eight slots per cache line:
//
//   [63:49] 15-bit tag   high bits of the hash; rejects a non-matching probe without touching the key
//   [48]    TOMB
//   [47:0]  KvObj*       boot verifies the allocator stays in the low 48-bit VA range; debug packs
//                       assert the same invariant before using the top bits
//
//   word == 0             EMPTY  the calloc state, and the ONLY thing that stops a probe
//   ptr != 0              LIVE
//   word != 0, ptr == 0   DEAD   tombstone; reusable, never stops a probe
//

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..54b7fdf93a8800a3dea3d561277ab0c13a3b45c6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/atomic_admission.h
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+// atomic_admission.h -- exact atomic-window accounting with bounded admission and retirement.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdlib>
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+class AtomicAdmissionCredits {
+public:
+    enum class Attempt { Admitted, Full, Contended };
+
+    void init(uint32_t window) { state_.store(pack(window, 0), std::memory_order_relaxed); }
+    uint32_t window() const { return limit(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+    uint32_t active() const { return used(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    bool can_admit() const { return has_room(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    Attempt try_admit() {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        if (!has_room(state)) return Attempt::Full;
+        // A failed reservation returns to the existing dispatch backpressure path. Strong CAS
+        // avoids spurious refusal; a competing admission, retirement or CONFIG can win only this
+        // attempt, never make the connection-owning thread spin on its behalf.
+        return state_.compare_exchange_strong(state, state + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                              std::memory_order_relaxed)
+            ? Attempt::Admitted : Attempt::Contended;
+    }
+
+    void retire() {
+        if (!used(state_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel))) std::abort();
+    }
+
+    void set_window(uint32_t window) {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        while (!state_.compare_exchange_weak(state, pack(window, used(state)),
+                                             std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                             std::memory_order_acquire)) {}
+        // Only the setter retries. The word is always usable: a stopped setter owns no odd
+        // generation, lock or credit operation that an admitting/retiring reader must wait on.
+    }
+
+    uint32_t pool() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) > used(state) ? limit(state) - used(state) : 0;
+    }
+    uint32_t debt() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) && used(state) > limit(state) ? used(state) - limit(state) : 0;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static uint64_t pack(uint32_t window, uint32_t active) {
+        return (uint64_t{window} << 32) | active;
+    }
+    static uint32_t used(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state); }
+    static uint32_t limit(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state >> 32); }
+    static bool has_room(uint64_t state) {
+        // Unlimited still cannot overflow the representation. Exhaustion uses backpressure.
+        return used(state) != UINT32_MAX && (!limit(state) || used(state) < limit(state));
+    }
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> state_{pack(256, 0)};
+};
+static_assert(sizeof(AtomicAdmissionCredits) == sizeof(uint64_t));
+
+} // namespace tomo

+// live_config.h -- coherent configuration publication without reader retries or reclamation.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include "config.h"
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+struct LiveConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version;
+    uint64_t maxmemory;
+    MaxmemoryPolicy policy;
+    uint32_t samples;
+    uint32_t notify_events;
+    bool tracking_armed;
+    int64_t slowlog_log_slower_than;
+    uint32_t latency_monitor_threshold;
+    bool save_armed;
+    uint64_t proto_max_bulk_len;
+    uint32_t debug_fanout_defer_us;
+};
+
+struct ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version = 0;
+    uint32_t timeout = 0;
+    ClientBufferLimit normal{};
+    ClientBufferLimit pubsub{};
+};
+
+struct LiveConfigValues {
+    LiveConfigSnapshot live{};
+    ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot clients{};
+};
+
+// Exactly one consumer, identified by physical ThreadCtx id, and one serialized CONFIG producer.
+// They each own one slot; an atomic exchange transfers ownership of the third (middle) slot.
+// The producer never touches the consumer's slot, even if that worker stops indefinitely.
+// No slot is freed, no reader announces a grace period, and no operation retries an exchange.
+class LiveConfigMailbox {
+public:
+    void init(const LiveConfigValues& initial) {
+        for (auto& slot : slots_) slot = {initial, initial};
+    }
+
+    void publish(const LiveConfigValues& previous, const LiveConfigValues& next) {
+        slots_[back_] = {previous, next};
+        back_ = middle_.exchange(back_ | kDirty, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+    }
+
+    const LiveConfigValues& read(const std::atomic<uint64_t>& version) {
+        if (middle_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & kDirty)
+            front_ = middle_.exchange(front_, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+        // CONFIG stages every mailbox before publishing the even version. During that staging
+        // interval choose the preceding committed value, not the partly published new version.
+        // Load AFTER acquiring the slot: its publication also orders CONFIG's odd version store,
+        // so this load cannot precede the commit of slot.previous. Keep both values even if this
+        // consumer acquires an uncommitted slot and the writer then stops before committing it.
+        const uint64_t committed = version.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & ~uint64_t{1};
+        const auto& slot = slots_[front_];
+        return slot.next.live.version <= committed ? slot.next : slot.previous;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static constexpr uint32_t kDirty = 4;
+    static constexpr uint32_t kIndex = 3;
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    struct Publication {
+        LiveConfigValues previous;
+        LiveConfigValues next;
+    };
+    Publication slots_[3]{};
+    alignas(64) uint32_t front_ = 0;                  // consumer only
+    alignas(64) uint32_t back_ = 1;                   // serialized producer only
+    alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> middle_{2};
+};
+
+} // namespace tomo

+        return limit(state) && used(state) > limit(state) ? used(state) - limit(state) : 0;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static uint64_t pack(uint32_t window, uint32_t active) {
+        return (uint64_t{window} << 32) | active;
+    }
+    static uint32_t used(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state); }
+    static uint32_t limit(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state >> 32); }
+    static bool has_room(uint64_t state) {
+        // Unlimited still cannot overflow the representation. Exhaustion uses backpressure.
+        return used(state) != UINT32_MAX && (!limit(state) || used(state) < limit(state));
+    }
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> state_{pack(256, 0)};
+};
+static_assert(sizeof(AtomicAdmissionCredits) == sizeof(uint64_t));
+
+} // namespace tomo

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..ced0fbb1b9db8ede852e773a25826654020de3a1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/live_config.h
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// live_config.h -- coherent configuration publication without reader retries or reclamation.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include "config.h"
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+struct LiveConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version;
+    uint64_t maxmemory;
+    MaxmemoryPolicy policy;
+    uint32_t samples;
+    uint32_t notify_events;
+    bool tracking_armed;
+    int64_t slowlog_log_slower_than;
+    uint32_t latency_monitor_threshold;
+    bool save_armed;
+    uint64_t proto_max_bulk_len;
+    uint32_t debug_fanout_defer_us;
+};
+
+struct ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version = 0;
+    uint32_t timeout = 0;
+    ClientBufferLimit normal{};
+    ClientBufferLimit pubsub{};
+};
+
+struct LiveConfigValues {
+    LiveConfigSnapshot live{};
+    ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot clients{};
+};
+
+// Exactly one consumer, identified by physical ThreadCtx id, and one serialized CONFIG producer.
+// They each own one slot; an atomic exchange transfers ownership of the third (middle) slot.
+// The producer never touches the consumer's slot, even if that worker stops indefinitely.
+// No slot is freed, no reader announces a grace period, and no operation retries an exchange.
+class LiveConfigMailbox {
+public:
+    void init(const LiveConfigValues& initial) {
+        for (auto& slot : slots_) slot = {initial, initial};
+    }
+
+    void publish(const LiveConfigValues& previous, const LiveConfigValues& next) {
+        slots_[back_] = {previous, next};
+        back_ = middle_.exchange(back_ | kDirty, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+    }
+
+    const LiveConfigValues& read(const std::atomic<uint64_t>& version) {
+        if (middle_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & kDirty)
+            front_ = middle_.exchange(front_, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+        // CONFIG stages every mailbox before publishing the even version. During that staging
+        // interval choose the preceding committed value, not the partly published new version.
+        // Load AFTER acquiring the slot: its publication also orders CONFIG's odd version store,
+        // so this load cannot precede the commit of slot.previous. Keep both values even if this
+        // consumer acquires an uncommitted slot and the writer then stops before committing it.
+        const uint64_t committed = version.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & ~uint64_t{1};
+        const auto& slot = slots_[front_];
+        return slot.next.live.version <= committed ? slot.next : slot.previous;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static constexpr uint32_t kDirty = 4;
+    static constexpr uint32_t kIndex = 3;
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    struct Publication {
+        LiveConfigValues previous;
+        LiveConfigValues next;
+    };
+    Publication slots_[3]{};
+    alignas(64) uint32_t front_ = 0;                  // consumer only
+    alignas(64) uint32_t back_ = 1;                   // serialized producer only
+    alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> middle_{2};
+};
+
+} // namespace tomo

diff --git a/src/core/atomic_admission.h b/src/core/atomic_admission.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..54b7fdf93a8800a3dea3d561277ab0c13a3b45c6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/atomic_admission.h
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+// atomic_admission.h -- exact atomic-window accounting with bounded admission and retirement.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdlib>
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+class AtomicAdmissionCredits {
+public:
+    enum class Attempt { Admitted, Full, Contended };
+
+    void init(uint32_t window) { state_.store(pack(window, 0), std::memory_order_relaxed); }
+    uint32_t window() const { return limit(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+    uint32_t active() const { return used(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    bool can_admit() const { return has_room(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    Attempt try_admit() {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        if (!has_room(state)) return Attempt::Full;
+        // A failed reservation returns to the existing dispatch backpressure path. Strong CAS
+        // avoids spurious refusal; a competing admission, retirement or CONFIG can win only this
+        // attempt, never make the connection-owning thread spin on its behalf.
+        return state_.compare_exchange_strong(state, state + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                              std::memory_order_relaxed)
+            ? Attempt::Admitted : Attempt::Contended;
+    }
+
+    void retire() {
+        if (!used(state_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel))) std::abort();
+    }
+
+    void set_window(uint32_t window) {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        while (!state_.compare_exchange_weak(state, pack(window, used(state)),
+                                             std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                             std::memory_order_acquire)) {}
+        // Only the setter retries. The word is always usable: a stopped setter owns no odd
+        // generation, lock or credit operation that an admitting/retiring reader must wait on.
+    }
+
+    uint32_t pool() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) > used(state) ? limit(state) - used(state) : 0;
+    }
+    uint32_t debt() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) && used(state) > limit(state) ? used(state) - limit(state) : 0;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static uint64_t pack(uint32_t window, uint32_t active) {
+        return (uint64_t{window} << 32) | active;
+    }
+    static uint32_t used(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state); }
+    static uint32_t limit(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state >> 32); }
+    static bool has_room(uint64_t state) {
+        // Unlimited still cannot overflow the representation. Exhaustion uses backpressure.
+        return used(state) != UINT32_MAX && (!limit(state) || used(state) < limit(state));
+    }
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> state_{pack(256, 0)};
+};
+static_assert(sizeof(AtomicAdmissionCredits) == sizeof(uint64_t));
+
+} // namespace tomo

+// live_config.h -- coherent configuration publication without reader retries or reclamation.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include "config.h"
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+struct LiveConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version;
+    uint64_t maxmemory;
+    MaxmemoryPolicy policy;
+    uint32_t samples;
+    uint32_t notify_events;
+    bool tracking_armed;
+    int64_t slowlog_log_slower_than;
+    uint32_t latency_monitor_threshold;
+    bool save_armed;
+    uint64_t proto_max_bulk_len;
+    uint32_t debug_fanout_defer_us;
+};
+
+struct ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version = 0;
+    uint32_t timeout = 0;
+    ClientBufferLimit normal{};
+    ClientBufferLimit pubsub{};
+};
+
+struct LiveConfigValues {
+    LiveConfigSnapshot live{};
+    ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot clients{};
+};
+
+// Exactly one consumer, identified by physical ThreadCtx id, and one serialized CONFIG producer.
+// They each own one slot; an atomic exchange transfers ownership of the third (middle) slot.
+// The producer never touches the consumer's slot, even if that worker stops indefinitely.
+// No slot is freed, no reader announces a grace period, and no operation retries an exchange.
+class LiveConfigMailbox {
+public:
+    void init(const LiveConfigValues& initial) {
+        for (auto& slot : slots_) slot = {initial, initial};
+    }
+
+    void publish(const LiveConfigValues& previous, const LiveConfigValues& next) {
+        slots_[back_] = {previous, next};
+        back_ = middle_.exchange(back_ | kDirty, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+    }
+
+    const LiveConfigValues& read(const std::atomic<uint64_t>& version) {
+        if (middle_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & kDirty)
+            front_ = middle_.exchange(front_, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+        // CONFIG stages every mailbox before publishing the even version. During that staging
+        // interval choose the preceding committed value, not the partly published new version.
+        // Load AFTER acquiring the slot: its publication also orders CONFIG's odd version store,
+        // so this load cannot precede the commit of slot.previous. Keep both values even if this
+        // consumer acquires an uncommitted slot and the writer then stops before committing it.
+        const uint64_t committed = version.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & ~uint64_t{1};
+        const auto& slot = slots_[front_];
+        return slot.next.live.version <= committed ? slot.next : slot.previous;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static constexpr uint32_t kDirty = 4;
+    static constexpr uint32_t kIndex = 3;
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    struct Publication {
+        LiveConfigValues previous;
+        LiveConfigValues next;
+    };
+    Publication slots_[3]{};
+    alignas(64) uint32_t front_ = 0;                  // consumer only
+    alignas(64) uint32_t back_ = 1;                   // serialized producer only
+    alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> middle_{2};
+};
+
+} // namespace tomo

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..54b7fdf93a8800a3dea3d561277ab0c13a3b45c6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/atomic_admission.h
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+// atomic_admission.h -- exact atomic-window accounting with bounded admission and retirement.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdlib>
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+class AtomicAdmissionCredits {
+public:
+    enum class Attempt { Admitted, Full, Contended };
+
+    void init(uint32_t window) { state_.store(pack(window, 0), std::memory_order_relaxed); }
+    uint32_t window() const { return limit(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+    uint32_t active() const { return used(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    bool can_admit() const { return has_room(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    Attempt try_admit() {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        if (!has_room(state)) return Attempt::Full;
+        // A failed reservation returns to the existing dispatch backpressure path. Strong CAS
+        // avoids spurious refusal; a competing admission, retirement or CONFIG can win only this
+        // attempt, never make the connection-owning thread spin on its behalf.
+        return state_.compare_exchange_strong(state, state + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                              std::memory_order_relaxed)
+            ? Attempt::Admitted : Attempt::Contended;
+    }
+
+    void retire() {
+        if (!used(state_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel))) std::abort();
+    }
+
+    void set_window(uint32_t window) {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        while (!state_.compare_exchange_weak(state, pack(window, used(state)),
+                                             std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                             std::memory_order_acquire)) {}
+        // Only the setter retries. The word is always usable: a stopped setter owns no odd
+        // generation, lock or credit operation that an admitting/retiring reader must wait on.
+    }
+
+    uint32_t pool() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) > used(state) ? limit(state) - used(state) : 0;
+    }
+    uint32_t debt() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) && used(state) > limit(state) ? used(state) - limit(state) : 0;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static uint64_t pack(uint32_t window, uint32_t active) {
+        return (uint64_t{window} << 32) | active;
+    }
+    static uint32_t used(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state); }
+    static uint32_t limit(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state >> 32); }
+    static bool has_room(uint64_t state) {
+        // Unlimited still cannot overflow the representation. Exhaustion uses backpressure.
+        return used(state) != UINT32_MAX && (!limit(state) || used(state) < limit(state));
+    }
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> state_{pack(256, 0)};
+};
+static_assert(sizeof(AtomicAdmissionCredits) == sizeof(uint64_t));
+
+} // namespace tomo

@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// live_config.h -- coherent configuration publication without reader retries or reclamation.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include "config.h"
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+struct LiveConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version;
+    uint64_t maxmemory;
+    MaxmemoryPolicy policy;
+    uint32_t samples;
+    uint32_t notify_events;
+    bool tracking_armed;
+    int64_t slowlog_log_slower_than;
+    uint32_t latency_monitor_threshold;
+    bool save_armed;
+    uint64_t proto_max_bulk_len;
+    uint32_t debug_fanout_defer_us;
+};
+
+struct ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version = 0;
+    uint32_t timeout = 0;
+    ClientBufferLimit normal{};
+    ClientBufferLimit pubsub{};
+};
+
+struct LiveConfigValues {
+    LiveConfigSnapshot live{};
+    ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot clients{};
+};
+
+// Exactly one consumer, identified by physical ThreadCtx id, and one serialized CONFIG producer.
+// They each own one slot; an atomic exchange transfers ownership of the third (middle) slot.
+// The producer never touches the consumer's slot, even if that worker stops indefinitely.
+// No slot is freed, no reader announces a grace period, and no operation retries an exchange.
+class LiveConfigMailbox {
+public:
+    void init(const LiveConfigValues& initial) {
+        for (auto& slot : slots_) slot = {initial, initial};
+    }
+
+    void publish(const LiveConfigValues& previous, const LiveConfigValues& next) {
+        slots_[back_] = {previous, next};
+        back_ = middle_.exchange(back_ | kDirty, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+    }
+
+    const LiveConfigValues& read(const std::atomic<uint64_t>& version) {
+        if (middle_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & kDirty)
+            front_ = middle_.exchange(front_, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+        // CONFIG stages every mailbox before publishing the even version. During that staging
+        // interval choose the preceding committed value, not the partly published new version.
+        // Load AFTER acquiring the slot: its publication also orders CONFIG's odd version store,
+        // so this load cannot precede the commit of slot.previous. Keep both values even if this
+        // consumer acquires an uncommitted slot and the writer then stops before committing it.
+        const uint64_t committed = version.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & ~uint64_t{1};
+        const auto& slot = slots_[front_];
+        return slot.next.live.version <= committed ? slot.next : slot.previous;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static constexpr uint32_t kDirty = 4;
+    static constexpr uint32_t kIndex = 3;
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    struct Publication {
+        LiveConfigValues previous;
+        LiveConfigValues next;
+    };
+    Publication slots_[3]{};
+    alignas(64) uint32_t front_ = 0;                  // consumer only
+    alignas(64) uint32_t back_ = 1;                   // serialized producer only
+    alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> middle_{2};
+};
+
+} // namespace tomo

+// atomic_admission.h -- exact atomic-window accounting with bounded admission and retirement.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdlib>
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+class AtomicAdmissionCredits {
+public:
+    enum class Attempt { Admitted, Full, Contended };
+
+    void init(uint32_t window) { state_.store(pack(window, 0), std::memory_order_relaxed); }
+    uint32_t window() const { return limit(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+    uint32_t active() const { return used(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    bool can_admit() const { return has_room(state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)); }
+
+    Attempt try_admit() {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        if (!has_room(state)) return Attempt::Full;
+        // A failed reservation returns to the existing dispatch backpressure path. Strong CAS
+        // avoids spurious refusal; a competing admission, retirement or CONFIG can win only this
+        // attempt, never make the connection-owning thread spin on its behalf.
+        return state_.compare_exchange_strong(state, state + 1, std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                              std::memory_order_relaxed)
+            ? Attempt::Admitted : Attempt::Contended;
+    }
+
+    void retire() {
+        if (!used(state_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel))) std::abort();
+    }
+
+    void set_window(uint32_t window) {
+        uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        while (!state_.compare_exchange_weak(state, pack(window, used(state)),
+                                             std::memory_order_acq_rel,
+                                             std::memory_order_acquire)) {}
+        // Only the setter retries. The word is always usable: a stopped setter owns no odd
+        // generation, lock or credit operation that an admitting/retiring reader must wait on.
+    }
+
+    uint32_t pool() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) > used(state) ? limit(state) - used(state) : 0;
+    }
+    uint32_t debt() const {
+        const uint64_t state = state_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
+        return limit(state) && used(state) > limit(state) ? used(state) - limit(state) : 0;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static uint64_t pack(uint32_t window, uint32_t active) {
+        return (uint64_t{window} << 32) | active;
+    }
+    static uint32_t used(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state); }
+    static uint32_t limit(uint64_t state) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(state >> 32); }
+    static bool has_room(uint64_t state) {
+        // Unlimited still cannot overflow the representation. Exhaustion uses backpressure.
+        return used(state) != UINT32_MAX && (!limit(state) || used(state) < limit(state));
+    }
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint64_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    std::atomic<uint64_t> state_{pack(256, 0)};
+};
+static_assert(sizeof(AtomicAdmissionCredits) == sizeof(uint64_t));
+
+} // namespace tomo
diff --git a/src/core/live_config.h b/src/core/live_config.h
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..ced0fbb1b9db8ede852e773a25826654020de3a1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/core/live_config.h
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// live_config.h -- coherent configuration publication without reader retries or reclamation.
+#pragma once
+#include <atomic>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include "config.h"
+
+namespace tomo {
+
+struct LiveConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version;
+    uint64_t maxmemory;
+    MaxmemoryPolicy policy;
+    uint32_t samples;
+    uint32_t notify_events;
+    bool tracking_armed;
+    int64_t slowlog_log_slower_than;
+    uint32_t latency_monitor_threshold;
+    bool save_armed;
+    uint64_t proto_max_bulk_len;
+    uint32_t debug_fanout_defer_us;
+};
+
+struct ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot {
+    uint64_t version = 0;
+    uint32_t timeout = 0;
+    ClientBufferLimit normal{};
+    ClientBufferLimit pubsub{};
+};
+
+struct LiveConfigValues {
+    LiveConfigSnapshot live{};
+    ClientLimitsConfigSnapshot clients{};
+};
+
+// Exactly one consumer, identified by physical ThreadCtx id, and one serialized CONFIG producer.
+// They each own one slot; an atomic exchange transfers ownership of the third (middle) slot.
+// The producer never touches the consumer's slot, even if that worker stops indefinitely.
+// No slot is freed, no reader announces a grace period, and no operation retries an exchange.
+class LiveConfigMailbox {
+public:
+    void init(const LiveConfigValues& initial) {
+        for (auto& slot : slots_) slot = {initial, initial};
+    }
+
+    void publish(const LiveConfigValues& previous, const LiveConfigValues& next) {
+        slots_[back_] = {previous, next};
+        back_ = middle_.exchange(back_ | kDirty, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+    }
+
+    const LiveConfigValues& read(const std::atomic<uint64_t>& version) {
+        if (middle_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & kDirty)
+            front_ = middle_.exchange(front_, std::memory_order_acq_rel) & kIndex;
+        // CONFIG stages every mailbox before publishing the even version. During that staging
+        // interval choose the preceding committed value, not the partly published new version.
+        // Load AFTER acquiring the slot: its publication also orders CONFIG's odd version store,
+        // so this load cannot precede the commit of slot.previous. Keep both values even if this
+        // consumer acquires an uncommitted slot and the writer then stops before committing it.
+        const uint64_t committed = version.load(std::memory_order_acquire) & ~uint64_t{1};
+        const auto& slot = slots_[front_];
+        return slot.next.live.version <= committed ? slot.next : slot.previous;
+    }
+
+private:
+    static constexpr uint32_t kDirty = 4;
+    static constexpr uint32_t kIndex = 3;
+    static_assert(std::atomic<uint32_t>::is_always_lock_free);
+    struct Publication {
+        LiveConfigValues previous;
+        LiveConfigValues next;
+    };
+    Publication slots_[3]{};
+    alignas(64) uint32_t front_ = 0;                  // consumer only
+    alignas(64) uint32_t back_ = 1;                   // serialized producer only
+    alignas(64) std::atomic<uint32_t> middle_{2};
+};
+
+} // namespace tomo

// read_local_reclaim.h — type-erased handoff from a shard store to its fused owner QSBR list.
//
// FlatStore cannot depend on ExLoop without reversing the core/store include graph. The store
// therefore publishes only this tiny boot-bound sink. Reclamation always runs later on the same
// physical owner thread; `owner` and `payload` are opaque until the callback is invoked after a
// grace period.
#pragma once
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include "read_local_settax.h"

namespace tomo {

struct KvBlockCache;

// Capacity of the owner's deferred-retire ring (ReadLocalRetireRing, src/core/read_local.h), which
// static_asserts that it still equals this number. It lives here because the store side derives a
// bound from it and cannot include a core/ header: the ring already permits exactly this many
// retired-but-unreclaimed objects to be resident per owner, so it is the natural ceiling for any
// cache of blocks that ring produces (see KvBlockCache::kMaxBytes).
inline constexpr uint32_t kReadLocalRetireRingCapacity = 4096;

struct ReadLocalRetireSink {
    using ReclaimFn = void (*)(const ReadLocalRetireSink& sink, void* owner,
                               void* payload, size_t auxiliary);
    using DeferFn = void (*)(void* context, void* owner, void* payload,
                            size_t auxiliary, ReclaimFn reclaim);

    void* context = nullptr;
    DeferFn defer = nullptr;
    // The owner's post-grace block cache (src/store/kv_block_cache.h). A DIRECT pointer, not a
    // third function pointer: the armed write path calls into it on every SET, and an indirect
    // call there would hand back part of the allocator call it exists to remove. Null means the
    // owner has no cache and every write allocates, which is the pre-cache behaviour.
    KvBlockCache* block_cache = nullptr;
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
    ReadLocalSetTaxStats* settax_stats = nullptr;
#endif

    void retire(void* owner, void* payload, size_t auxiliary, ReclaimFn reclaim) const {
        defer(context, owner, payload, auxiliary, reclaim);
    }

    void bind_settax_stats(ReadLocalSetTaxStats* stats) {
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
        settax_stats = stats;
#else
        (void)stats;
#endif
    }
    ReadLocalSetTaxStats* diagnostics() const {
#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT == 3
        return settax_stats;
#else
        return nullptr;
#endif
    }
};

#if TOMO_READ_LOCAL_SET_TAX_VARIANT != 3
static_assert(sizeof(ReadLocalRetireSink) == 3 * sizeof(void*),
              "the shipped retire sink is context + defer + block cache and nothing else");
#endif

}  // namespace tomo
CXX      ?= g++
JEDIR    ?= /home/user/Projects/refs/jemalloc/_install
# jemalloc is optional: without it the tree still builds and runs, using the deterministic portable
# size-class table in alloc.h. Set JE=0 to force that path (useful for A/B-ing the allocator).
JE       ?= 1
ifeq ($(JE),1)
  # Prefer the system package; fall back to the copy built from refs/.
  ifneq ($(wildcard /usr/include/jemalloc/jemalloc.h),)
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC
    JELIBS  := -ljemalloc
  else
    JEFLAGS := -DTOMO_JEMALLOC -I$(JEDIR)/include
    JELIBS  := $(JEDIR)/lib/libjemalloc.a -ldl
  endif
else
  JEFLAGS :=
  JELIBS  :=
endif
CXXFLAGS ?= -std=c++20 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -march=native -pthread
LDLIBS   ?= -luring -pthread
